title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: price increase
drivers.evidence: Price rose 6.2% to $12.03. Prior week (2026-09-28) sold 13 units (81% of baseline), and historical promotions show 10-30% discounts produce 29-124% lifts. A 6.2% price increase implies ~15-20% demand drop. Only one past week at this price, so effect shrunk.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 16.0. The target week has a 6.2% price increase to $12.03, which is above the regular $11.33. Historical data shows no past promotions at this price point, but a 30% off promotion in 2024-06-03 (x2.47) and 2024-12-30 (x2.25) had strong lifts. However, a 30% off in 2026-03-16 (x1.24) and a 10% off in 2025-07-28 (x1.29) had weaker effects. The noise-adjusted promotion lift is x1.39. Since this is a price increase, demand is expected to drop. The prior week (2026-09-28) sold 13 units at $12.03—13/16 = 0.81. This suggests a price sensitivity effect. The classical model's 1.00 is too high. A price rise of 6.2% likely reduces sales by ~15-20%, so median multiplier = 0.85. Spread widened slightly due to uncertainty in price response. No event or promotion. The 2026-09-28 week is the only data point at this price, so confidence is medium.

brief:
PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-11 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 16.0 | 5%-95%: 4.6 - 31.7 | 10%-90%: 6.2 - 28.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
